document: The Australian Prudential Regulation Authority supervises authorised deposit-taking institutions, general insurers, life insurers, private health insurers and most superannuation funds. Prudential standards address capital adequacy, liquidity, governance, risk management and operational resilience.
summary: APRA supervises banks, insurers and most super funds through prudential standards on capital, liquidity, governance and risk.

document: Fringe benefits tax is paid by employers on certain benefits provided to employees or their associates in place of salary or wages. The FBT year runs from 1 April to 31 March, which differs from the income tax year. Common fringe benefits include the private use of a work car, low-interest loans and paying an employee's private health insurance. The FBT rate is 47 percent, equal to the top marginal tax rate plus the Medicare levy, and is applied to the grossed-up taxable value of benefits.
summary: Employers pay FBT at 47 percent on non-cash benefits given to employees, in a year running from April to March.

document: The goods and services tax applies to taxable supplies made for consideration in the course of an enterprise connected with the indirect tax zone. Input-taxed supplies, such as residential rent and most financial supplies, do not attract GST, and the supplier cannot claim input tax credits for acquisitions relating to them.
summary: GST applies to taxable supplies made in an enterprise, but input-taxed supplies such as residential rent carry no GST and no input tax credits.

document: An employee is protected from unfair dismissal if they have completed the minimum employment period and either earn less than the high income threshold or are covered by an award or enterprise agreement. A dismissal is unfair if it was harsh, unjust or unreasonable and was not a case of genuine redundancy.
summary: Employees who have served the minimum period and are under the income threshold or covered by an award are protected from harsh, unjust or unreasonable dismissal.

document: Enterprise bargaining allows employers, employees and their bargaining representatives to negotiate an agreement tailored to a particular workplace. Bargaining representatives must meet good faith bargaining requirements, including attending meetings, disclosing relevant information in a timely manner and responding to proposals.
summary: Enterprise bargaining lets workplaces negotiate tailored agreements, with bargaining representatives bound by good faith requirements.

document: Employees with at least twelve months of continuous service can request flexible working arrangements if they are a parent of a school-age child, a carer, have a disability, are 55 or older, are pregnant, or are experiencing family and domestic violence. The request must be in writing, and the employer must respond in writing within 21 days. An employer can only refuse on reasonable business grounds after genuinely trying to reach agreement. Disputes about refusals can be dealt with by the Fair Work Commission.
summary: Eligible employees can request flexible work in writing, and employers must respond within 21 days and refuse only on reasonable business grounds.

document: Goods and services tax is a broad-based tax of 10 percent on most goods, services and other items sold or consumed in Australia. A business must register for GST when its GST turnover is $75,000 or more, while non-profit organisations have a higher threshold of $150,000. Taxi and ride-sourcing drivers must register regardless of turnover. Registered businesses report GST on their business activity statement and can generally claim credits for the GST included in the price of business purchases.
summary: GST is a 10 percent tax that businesses must register for once turnover reaches $75,000, with credits available for business purchases.

document: Under the National Employment Standards, full-time and part-time employees accrue four weeks of paid annual leave for each year of service, with shift workers entitled to an additional week. Annual leave accumulates progressively according to ordinary hours of work and carries over from year to year. Casual employees do not receive paid annual leave but are compensated through a casual loading, which is commonly 25 percent. Many modern awards also provide an annual leave loading of 17.5 percent.
summary: Employees accrue four weeks of paid annual leave a year, while casuals receive a loading instead.

document: A capital gain or loss arises when a CGT event happens, most commonly the sale of an asset such as shares or an investment property. Individuals and trusts that hold an asset for at least twelve months before the CGT event can reduce the capital gain by 50 percent, while complying superannuation funds receive a discount of one-third. Companies are not entitled to the CGT discount. Capital losses can only be offset against capital gains and may be carried forward indefinitely.
summary: Individuals and trusts holding assets for twelve months get a 50 percent CGT discount, super funds get one-third and companies get none.

document: The market integrity rules supplement the Corporations Act by setting out requirements for market participants on licensed financial markets. Insider trading occurs when a person in possession of inside information trades in, or procures another person to trade in, the relevant financial products.
summary: Market integrity rules add requirements for market participants, and insider trading means trading on inside information.

document: An employee who believes they were unfairly dismissed can apply to the Fair Work Commission. The application must be made within 21 days after the dismissal took effect. To be protected, an employee generally needs to have completed a minimum employment period of six months, or twelve months if the employer is a small business with fewer than fifteen employees. The Commission may order reinstatement or, where reinstatement is inappropriate, compensation capped at six months of pay.
summary: Unfair dismissal claims go to the Fair Work Commission within 21 days and may lead to reinstatement or capped compensation.

document: An Australian financial services licence is required to carry on a financial services business in Australia. Licensees must comply with general obligations, including having adequate resources, maintaining competence, having adequate risk management systems and a dispute resolution system that includes membership of the external complaints authority.
summary: Financial services businesses need an Australian financial services licence and must meet obligations on resources, competence, risk management and dispute resolution.
